A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ceftazidame avibactam resistance in K. pneumoniae isolates can be conferred through the acquisition of blaKPC-encoding genes that encode extended-spectrum β lactamases.
ceftazidame-avibactan is a promising new agent for treating infections caused by KPC-3 producers, but the potential for the emergence of resistance is high.
blaKPC-2 and blaKPC-4 encode the most clinically relevant variants, whereas blaKPC-5 and blaKPC variants with mutations in the Ω-loop are of limited clinical significance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KPC-3 is a highly promiscuous enzyme that can readily acquire resistance to ceftazidimes and ceftazidim-avibactams.

the blaKPC-2 and blaKPC-4 genes, which have been shown to encode extended-spectrum β lactamases, are also present in the genomes of ceftazidine-avibactum-resistant clinical Klebsella pneumoniae isolats.
the KPC-3 variant with D179Y/T241M substitutions, which has been reported in the literature as a blaKPC-2 mutation, is actually a blaKPC mutation.
